key_insight: The paper reframes OAM propagation as logical-qubit evolution through noisy channels, showing that turbulence causes structured leakage outside the logical OAM subspace that can be characterized and exploited for robust feature extraction.
engineering_relevance: This provides a physics-informed approach for making OAM-based quantum communication and sensing more robust to turbulence and channel imperfections, while enabling better characterization of degraded optical states.
method: Model OAM modes as logical qubits undergoing noisy quantum-channel evolution.
Identify turbulence-induced leakage signatures as a function of turbulence strength and OAM order.
Use distributed quantum feature extraction with quantum convolutional operations to learn turbulence-robust features.
evidence_signal: Simulations and experimental measurements show robust feature extraction across a broad range of turbulence strengths, OAM orders, and propagation conditions.
watch_item: The approach relies on accurate mapping of physical OAM dynamics to the logical-qubit model, so performance may depend on how well the channel and leakage processes are calibrated in practice.
paper_title: Structured leakage in OAM-encoded qubits revealed by distributed quantum feature extraction
